annotation: Initial start: Winter semester 2023/24 The digitisation of the economy, geopolitical changes and increasing cost pressure are having enormous impacts on the logistics and supply chain industry. Companies are therefore constantly looking for experts who can deal with this digital transformation and gain insights from large amounts of data in order to develop innovative supply chain solutions and business strategies. Take on these challenges and become part of a new generation of supply chain managers that knows how to deal with innovative digital solutions and complex SCM platforms and works confidently in a global and diverse environment. In the degree course, you will get to know the most important supply chain concepts, digital tools and their application. You will learn more about Supply Chain Management 4.0, innovation management, process management and big data and will be versed in current topics such as business intelligence, digital transformation and operations research. The use and customisation of SAP, the leading enterprise resource planning system, is just as familiar to you as programming apps. In addition, you will expand your knowledge of platform economics and digital business models and apply agile methods in study projects. Thanks to the project and skill-based approach, you will also develop your leadership, communication and intercultural skills and are therefore optimally prepared for demanding and international positions in digital supply chain management.

Oriented to the basic concept of systems engineering, students acquire technical know-how at the cutting edge of research and application skills for practical astronautics-related projects on concrete technical systems (e.g. satellite systems). Supplemented by management and social skills, the aim is to take the constantly increasing complexity of software-intensive technical systems in the space industry into account. The degree course is designed as a strategic cooperation with the Gdańsk University of Technology. The study programme concept provides for one theoretical semester to be completed in Gdańsk and one in Bremen and for the credits earned to be credited to the curricula of the respective study programmes at both universities to enable students to obtain two degrees as a ‘double degree’.

For the mobility of the future, more and more functions are being implemented via software in modern vehicles. In some cases, more than 200 control units are installed in a vehicle and up to 16 gigabytes of software data are imported. Software is therefore a crucial key component, which is why the industry is now talking about Software Defined Vehicles (SDV). This development requires highly complex systems with hardware and software components for more and more safety, comfort and entertainment on board, which in turn requires highly qualified experts for development and implementation.

annotation: Why study Industrial Artificial Intelligence IAI? The teaching language of the Industrial Artificial Intelligence degree programme is English. IAI is for people who are interested in all aspects of artificial intelligence and want to play an active role in shaping the topic of artificial intelligence. You will effectively link the relevant industrial business areas with artificial intelligence, recognise efficiency potential and implement your findings in practical projects with companies. Learning by doing will lead you to success in this project-oriented degree programme. AI technology is changing the world of work: ‘By 2030, around 30% of current working hours could be automated by technology, including generative AI’ (McKinsey Global Institute, 2025). All areas of companies will be affected, including production, logistics or supply chain, planning, purchasing, manufacturing or assembly and many more. The degree opens up excellent career opportunities in the industry, as experts in artificial intelligence are sought-after graduates in a rapidly growing market for artificial intelligence: according to Statista (2024), the market volume will increase from USD 96 billion in 2021 to an estimated USD 1.848 billion in 2030. What does the IAI Master’s programme look like? The programme combines theory and practice within the framework of projects. Learning by doing is at the centre of the course. Different specialisations are taught in each semester: - The Industrial Operation and Transformation specialisation deals with the relevant AI application areas and the associated, marketable AI tools that shape everyday practice - The Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering specialisation provides in-depth knowledge that enables you to independently develop and refine AI tools and thus make an important contribution beyond the practical application of tools. You will acquire comprehensive knowledge in AI-oriented Python programming, machine and deep learning as well as generative AI. You will also expand your knowledge of big data, data science and data engineering. This knowledge is supplemented by practical knowledge of application software packages from well-known manufacturers (e.g. Microsoft, SAP, Siemens, AWS), which deal with topics such as ERP systems, cloud computing, robotic process automation, business intelligence and analytics. Semester structure / programme content You will acquire comprehensive knowledge in AI-oriented Python programming, machine and deep learning as well as generative AI. You will also expand your knowledge of big data, data science and data engineering. This knowledge is supplemented by practical knowledge of application software packages from well-known manufacturers (e.g. Microsoft, SAP, Siemens, AWS), which deal with topics such as ERP systems, cloud computing, robotic process automation, business intelligence and analytics. Your future: What can you achieve with your degree? With your degree, you will have a wide range of career opportunities, some of which we cannot even fully assess today. In addition to the traditional areas of employment / job offers, there are also new areas of employment for IAI Master’s graduates that are being created by AI in companies. These include the following jobs: - AI engineer – These are responsible for integrating artificial intelligence into existing industrial systems or developing it for these systems themselves. - AI consultant – They carry out analyses and develop concepts for the introduction of AI technology and its application to increase costs and efficiency in industrial business areas. - AI business developer – Develops and implements AI/ML models and solutions for specific business challenges. - AI product manager – A specialist to oversee, create and manage products that utilise AI technologies. - AI research scientist – A professional who conducts research and development in the field of artificial intelligence.

annotation: High-integrity systems are complex, software-controlled systems. These systems protect people, the environment, organisations and society. They can be divided into two areas of application: - Safety-critical systems (SCS) have a direct impact on the life and health of humans and the environment. They are used in all industrial sectors, e.g. aerospace, automotive, railway and marine systems, power generation, medical technology, SCADA and others. - Mission-critical systems (MCS) have a high criticality with regard to the functioning of an organization, e.g. ERP, CRM and others. A Master's academic degree in High Integrity Systems opens up access to a wide range of professional opportunities in various areas of application in computer science. The development of software and IT services for high integrity systems is crucial for all industries, as well as administrative applications, banking and financial systems.
admissionRequirements: Admission requirements: - The Bachelor's or Diploma examination in a university degree course of at least six semesters worth a minimum of 180 ECTS credit points in Computer Science or in another degree course in which Computer Science accounts for at least 70 % of the ECTS credit points possible in this degree course. The grade of the certificate of academic degree must be at least 1.8. Applicants with a Bachelor's grade between 1.9 and 2.5 can be admitted as part of a special procedure if they can prove they have special qualifications. -English proficiency level B2 through a language test of the CEFR, not older than 3 years (e.g. TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge Certificate, DAAD) - Curriculum Vitae -Letter of motivation Further information can be found on the website of the degree course: https://www.frankfurt-university.de/de/studium/master-studiengange/high-integrity-systems-msc/fuer-studieninteressierte/
